FABLE 5 DROPPED 48 HOURS AGO. HERE’S WHAT PEOPLE ALREADY DID WITH IT.

→ 50M line Stripe codebase migrated in 1 day.
A full team needs 2 months.

→ Full game engine with physics + multiplayer.
10 minutes. One prompt.

→ 271 Firefox zero-days discovered autonomously.
And chained together.

→ McKinsey-style report from scratch.
One prompt. Pixel perfect.

This isn’t a model upgrade.

This is a different category entirely.

91/100 on Senior Engineer benchmark.
GPT-5.5 scored 62.

Free until June 22.

https://t.co/RbQjcGtbln → model picker → Fable 5.

Go. Now.

Claude Fable 5 (Mythos) will COOK game devs

Imagine building a full game using just prompts 💀

Model + animations are fully procedural via Three.js. Shaders (including foliage) were ported from personal projects by a redditor

I've seen guys build GTA-6 using Claude Code 😭

What else have people been building with Claude Fable?

this is purely claude fable in claude code, no other models, assets, or anything. it just threw this together with a few prompts.

i'm liking it so much i might genuinely develop this into a full game https://t.co/qLc7p4jJsJ

AI bros are out here acting like Claude Fable 5 just birthed the singularity. 

"It migrated a 50M line codebase!! Built a full game in one shot!!"

Bro. 99% of you are using it to:

- Summarize your emails
- Generate mid LinkedIn posts
- Ask it to roast your ex

Calm down. 
It's not curing cancer, it's curing your writer's block. 😂

The story: this started as a few hours of ideation with just the chatbot. Prototype, playtest, tear it down, rebuild. Once the feel was close, I ported it to my Mac mini for a proper local build.

Fable 5 wrote the handoff package. A full game design doc, a tech spec with an 11-phase build plan, and an instruction file telling Claude Code exactly how to work.

Then I let Claude Code build it. A few hours in, I discovered it had been running on Sonnet the whole time (doh!). So I rebuilt everything with Fable 5. All 11 phases in about an hour and a half.

This was the first playtest. Long way to go, but I'm really happy with the start.
